correctness.rationale: The affine charts are rigorously identified as rank-one matrix cones, with only the vertex singular. Segre degree and Picard/section-cone quotient yield multiplicities, local class groups and the canonical obstruction. The primitive 2n toric facet rays generate the full one-parameter lattice; all maximal-cone Cartier equations are solved integrally, giving Picard rank one and primitive O(1), free Cl of rank n+1 and quotient rank n. The -K compatibility is satisfied exactly for n=4; finite verifications are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The 2024 complete primary Second Hypersimplex section establishes the polytope, degree and principal A-determinant (Proposition 3.2, Theorem 3.6), not intrinsic isolated singularities, local rank-one cones, or integral global divisor groups. The 2026 motivating indexed abstract addresses Euler/ML stratifications; inaccessible full text is explicitly retained as a priority risk. Direct searches across hypersimplex, squarefree Veronese and local class-group aliases and public mathematical records produced closest matches with unrelated toric models or ML-degree invariants, not stronger statements implying this joint classification. This is a provisional priority assessment, not proof by failed search.
residual_risks: The relevant 2026 Oldekop preprint is potentially covering but could not be read in complete text; its abstract is insufficient for a whole-paper exclusion.
Equivalent classical squarefree-Veronese treatments may give some or all statements under a different name; targeted searches reduce but do not eliminate this risk.
No independent validation of the present all-n geometric proof has been performed.

value.rationale: A motivated and natural complete classification for the second-hypersimplex family currently used in Euler/ML stratification: every singular point and its full analytic cone, multiplicity, local Gorenstein obstruction, all global divisor groups and the exact n=4 to n=5 threshold. It is not an arbitrary finite invariant, a mere relabeling, or a re-computation of known ML-degree tables.
